channel.title: Sammamish Dispatch
channel.description: Sammamish news, once a week, from the Sammamish Dispatch.

item.title: Five public hearings are on the council's Tuesday, November 17 meeting, which starts at 6:30 PM
item.description: The city's notices list the 2027–28 budget and property tax levy (with potential adoption), the 2027–2032 Six-Year CIP, the Building 120 map change, the school districts' capital facilities plans, and a code amendment proposed in 2019 that is still outstanding.

item.title: The school fee hearing adopts three districts' plans, not just two
item.description: The council will consider three ordinances adopting the 2026–2031 capital facilities plans of the Issaquah, Lake Washington and Snoqualmie Valley school districts.

item.title: Volunteers plant a pollinator meadow at Evans Creek Preserve on Saturday, November 14, 11 AM to 2 PM
item.description: Crews will plant bulbs and wildflowers next to the existing pollinator site, part of the city's Bee City work.

item.title: where the generator goes
item.description: If you run a generator in an outage, keep it outdoors and more than 20 feet from windows, doors and vents, and never in the garage, even with the door open.

item.title: Why the power there goes out first and comes back last, and two more readers asked the same about parts of Sammamish
item.description: A reader south of Pine Lake asked why the power there goes out first and comes back last, and two more readers asked the same about parts of Sammamish.

item.title: The council's budget and levy hearings run to November 17
item.description: The budget page lists a public hearing on the 2027–28 budget and property tax levy at a November 4 special meeting, a November 5 placeholder for budget review, and a November 17 regular meeting with the hearing and potential adoption.

item.title: The Six-Year capital plan hearing is also November 17
item.description: The city's legal notices list a public hearing on the 2027–2032 Six-Year CIP document on the same night.

item.title: A November 17 hearing is set on file POL2025-00572, tied to Building 120
item.description: A notice of public hearing dated November 3 carries that file number and the name Building 120.

item.title: Stormwater pipe cameras are inspecting lines through Friday, November 6
item.description: Crews are working at 228th Avenue SE and SE 8th Street, SE 22nd Place, 210th Place SE, 212th Avenue SE and NE 26th Place.

item.title: a freeze plan before the cold
item.description: Before a hard freeze, open the cabinet doors under sinks on exterior walls so room heat reaches the pipes, and let an indoor faucet drip cold water.

item.title: When Ziply fiber will be connected in the streets there, about a year and a half after the conduit went in, as the reader describes it
item.description: A reader north of Inglewood asked when Ziply fiber will be connected in the streets there, about a year and a half after the conduit went in, as the reader describes it.

item.title: Second-half property taxes are due Monday, November 2
item.description: October 31 is a Saturday this year, so the deadline moves to the next business day.

item.title: Ballots for the November 3 general election are due by 8 PM Tuesday
item.description: Mail one postmarked by Election Day, or use a Vote Center or one of King County's 100 official drop boxes, which close at 8 PM sharp.

item.title: The budget's first public hearing is Wednesday, November 4
item.description: The special meeting takes testimony on the 2027–28 budget and the property tax levy, after this week's department presentations.

item.title: Three lane-closure jobs end this week
item.description: Tree trimming on 228th Avenue, Issaquah-Pine Lake Road to Sahalee Way, runs through Friday, October 30, as does stormwater-pipe camera work at 228th Avenue SE and SE 8th Street, SE 22nd Place and 212th Avenue SE. Weekend work on the George Davis Creek fish passage, East Lake Sammamish Parkway, ends…

item.title: Issaquah elementary students have no school November 4 and 5
item.description: Those are conference days.

item.title: clocks back, alarms tested
item.description: Daylight saving time ends at 2 AM Sunday, November 1, when clocks fall back an hour.

item.title: The proposed 2027–28 budget spends $220.3 million against $204.0 million in revenue
item.description: The $16.3 million gap comes from savings, almost all for one-time capital projects; no new debt is planned.

item.title: Council goes through the budget department by department October 27 and 28
item.description: Both special meetings run 6:30 to 9 PM at City Hall and open with public comment.

item.title: Building 120 goes to a council hearing November 17
item.description: The change would make the 21.5-acre city site at 120 228th Ave NE a Mixed Use Center, opening a rezone from R-6 to Community Business: up to 18 homes an acre instead of 6, and 60 feet of height instead of 35.

item.title: SE 32nd Street gets a new sidewalk and bike lane
item.description: For about eight weeks from October 19, crews build 630 feet of sidewalk and bike lane on the north side between 241st and 244th Avenues SE, weekdays, with flaggers.

item.title: The October 31 recycling list is out
item.description: At Eastside Catholic School, 9 AM to 3 PM: up to six passenger tires free, electronics, TVs, and lead-acid and alkaline batteries.

item.title: who handles what when a storm hits
item.description: Wind and rain bring down trees and power lines this time of year.

item.title: Building 120 reaches the council Tuesday, after tonight's Planning Commission hearing
item.description: The commission takes testimony at 6:30 PM on the map change for the 21.5-acre city site at 120 228th Ave NE. The council's long-range calendar puts a briefing at its 5:30 PM work session October 20 and the council's own hearing on November 17.

item.title: New homes in the Lake Washington district would pay $8,810.25 in school impact fees from January 1, down from $10,914.75
item.description: That rate covers single-family homes with three or more bedrooms; under the new bedroom-count formula, every other Lake Washington category drops to $0, and the Issaquah district stays at $0.

item.title: A 9.27-acre rezone off SE 1st Street goes to the hearing examiner Friday, October 23
item.description: Owners of four parcels at 214th Ave SE and SE 1st Street ask to move from R-1 (one home per acre) to R-4 (four per acre); city staff recommend approval.

item.title: The fall recycling and shredding event is Saturday, October 31, 9 AM to 3 PM, at Eastside Catholic School, 232 228th Ave SE
item.description: It is free; items with fees are cash only, and no vehicles enter after 3 PM. The city says the accepted-materials list is published closer to the date.

item.title: leaves belong in the cart, not the drain
item.description: Sammamish has about 12,000 storm drains, and fall leaves are what clog them.

item.title: Tree crews take one lane of 228th Avenue, 9:30 AM to 3:30 PM, from today through October 30
item.description: The work runs both directions from Issaquah-Pine Lake Road to the city limit on Sahalee Way; the city says to expect delays.

item.title: Building 120 gets a land-use hearing Thursday
item.description: The Planning Commission meets at 6:30 PM on October 15 in Council Chambers, City Hall, 801 228th Ave SE, and streams online.

item.title: The 2027–28 budget arrives October 20
item.description: The city manager presents the proposed two-year budget at the 6:30 PM council meeting that Tuesday; special budget sessions follow October 27 and 28, and the budget and property tax levy hearings are noticed for November 4.

item.title: No school Friday in Lake Washington schools; Issaquah schools are in session
item.description: Lake Washington School District has a LEAP day on October 16, and preschool programs pause October 13–15 for conferences.

item.title: Weekend work on East Lake Sammamish Parkway, every Saturday and Sunday through October 31
item.description: Crews on the George Davis Creek fish-passage project work 7 AM to 6 PM south of NE 7th Court, with a 20 mph limit and a posted detour map.

item.title: November 2, not October 31
item.description: The second half of 2026 King County property tax is due Monday, November 2.
